newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks lower, seen as falling further.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks lower, seen as falling further.

text.p: Croatian stocks were steady to lower on Wednesday, and traders said the end of the downward trend was not in sight in the absence of big buyers on the market.
"Small shareholders are no longer in a buying mood so the prices are falling," a trader at Metroholding brokerage said, adding:
"Only a big investor could reverse the current trend... small shareholders need that kind of encouragement."
He said only the fully-listed issues, Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva, would rather trace developments in London than in Zagreb.
Thursday's trading had one gainer only, with five issues closing lower and four remaining flat.
Turnover halved to 5.4 million kuna ($1 million) whereas volume shrank to 4,578 shares.
Istrian hotelier Riviera from Porec was the only issue closing higher on Thursday, but it only recovered 10 kuna to 230, after recording a 30 kuna loss the day before.

Other two active hoteliers, Jadranturist and Suncani Hvar both edged down. Jadranturist topped the list of decliners, losing 60 kuna to 280, on volume of 494 units. Suncani Hvar inched down six kuna to 64, trading 1,218 shares.
Pliva remained flat at 13,300 kuna on volume of 315 shares. Zagrebacka lost five kuna to 1,030, with 175 shares traded. Both were seen as rising in the near future.
The bank's E-series traded flat at 480 kuna, selling 252 shares. Trgovacka Banka and cable maker Elka also remained stable at 1,600 and 280 kuna respectively.
Confectioner Kras was among decliners, continuing its falling trend by losing another 20 kuna to 650 on volume of 340 shares.
Food processor Podravka was the most actively traded issue with 1,469 units sold, and inching down only 50 lipa to 268.
The central bank exchange rate firmed to 5.43012 to the dollar, up from 5.4566 on Wednesday. ($ = 5.392 Croatian Kuna)
